title: AI Engineering Without Borders — swyx
talk_summary: This is a keynote framing talk about what AI engineering is as a discipline, arguing that its 'borders' (track categories, definitions) are arbitrary human constructs and proposing 'laws' like improving context utilization and falling cost of intelligence.

takeaways.technique: Plan around declining cost of intelligence
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues AI engineers should internalize Moore's-law-like trends (context length/utilization improving, cost of intelligence falling) so they avoid bets that won't last.
takeaways.evidence_quote: in the past 2 years, we've seen a 99.55% decline in the cost of GPT-3 level intelligence
takeaways.numbers: 99.55% decline in cost of GPT-3-level intelligence over 2 years; ~80-90% decline for GPT-4-level

takeaways.technique: Track context utilization, not just window length
takeaways.what_they_do: Notes that long context is only useful if models actually utilize it well, citing Anthropic's improvements in utilization of long windows.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It's not just about the length of context, it's also about the utilization of context.
